# Primal, Unexploited Game-Design Ideas — and How They Could Land on Roblox
### A deep-research report · all-ages, international audience · the "could it have existed in 1935?" test
*Compiled 2026-06-06 from 5 parallel research agents (~110 sources). Claims tagged **[SOURCED]** / **[SPECULATION]** / **[CORRECTED]**.*

---

## The core thesis (what all five research threads converge on)

**The unexplored space in game design is gated by *ideas*, not *materials* or *technology*.** The most striking proof is **Yavalath (2007)** — a board game *generated by a computer program* (Cameron Browne's LUDI), whose rules ("place a stone on a hex grid; 4-in-a-row wins but 3-in-a-row loses") could have been drawn on a clay tablet 3,000 years ago, yet no human ever invented it. A machine searching the design space found a genuinely good game humans had missed. **[SOURCED]** (opinionatedgamers.com; iospress ICGA Journal)

This pattern repeats across the whole history of simple games:

| Genre / mechanic | Materially possible since | Actually invented | Lag |
|---|---|---|---|
| Connection games (**Hex**) | antiquity (grid + stones) | **1942** (Piet Hein) | ~millennia |
| Pencil topology (**Sprouts**) | paper existed | **1967** (Conway) | centuries |
| Nim's winning *theory* | played since antiquity | **1901** (Bouton) | millennia |
| **Worker placement** | tokens on spaces | **2005** (Caylus) | — |
| **Deck-building** | ordinary cards | **2008** (Dominion) | centuries |

**[SOURCED]** (Wikipedia: Hex / Sprouts / Nim / Caylus / Dominion)
> **[CORRECTED]** my brief guessed worker-placement at 2002 — that conflates *Puerto Rico*'s role-selection. Canonical origin is Keydom (1998) → Caylus (2005).

**Why the relational/social half of the space stays empty has a specific, citable cause** — Raph Koster's *plasticity filter*: a verb survives in game design only if it "confronts many, many situations." Combat, movement, and acquisition trivially generate situations, so they dominate; **care, gift, negotiate, teach, tend, reconcile** get filtered out *early* as "shallow," even though board games (Diplomacy, Chinatown) prove they sustain deep play. Daniel Cook calls the result an industry running on "habit, guesswork and slavish devotion to pre-existing form." **[SOURCED]** (raphkoster.com 2025; lostgarden.com)

The two historic blockers on the relational verbs — **(a)** you needed *human* counterparties (AI couldn't negotiate), and **(b)** asymmetric/social balance is hard — are exactly what a **massively-social UGC platform like Roblox dissolves**: it supplies the humans at scale. That's the strategic hinge of this whole report.

**And Roblox is literally paying for these gaps.** Its 2026 Incubator/Jumpstart programs fund under-represented genres (RPG, strategy, **social co-opetition**, "unexpected genre mash-ups") for its fast-aging audience: **27% of age-checked users are now 18+**, US 18–34 growing >50% YoY, and growth is overwhelmingly international (APAC ~36% of users; Japan +160%, Indonesia +700% YoY). The platform's own Q1-2024 search data shows **7.5M searches/quarter for "social co-opetition"** (board games, bingo, fashion — "working *with* others to solve or create") that supply doesn't meet. **[SOURCED]** (about.roblox.com newsroom 2024/2026; backlinko; sqmagazine)

---

## The ideas, ranked by the "1935 test" × Roblox fit

### TIER 1 — Strongest: primal, near-formless, and a natural fit for a social platform

---

#### 1. The **Cohabitive game** — non-zero-sum negotiation as the *entire* genre
**The single best-sourced "should exist but doesn't" finding in the sweep.**

- **The idea:** A third category beside competitive (zero-sum) and cooperative (shared win): you optimize *your own* outcome, but sabotaging others is never worth it. Pure bargaining and peace-craft — no hidden agendas, no forced betrayal. Designer "Screwtape" estimates it "should contain maybe a *third* of all the games I can imagine existing," yet it's nameless and nearly unpopulated; the only real prototype is Mako Yass's *Optimal Weave*, explicitly "the first of its kind." **[SOURCED]** (lesswrong.com/competitive-cooperative-and-cohabitive; dreamshrine.org/OW)
- **The 1935 test:** Splitting chores, dividing land, trading at a market — this *is* social life. It predates writing. A village in 1935 could have played it with tokens and a table.
- **Why unexploited:** Needs live humans who can talk and make deals — the historic AI-counterparty blocker. Board games solved it (Diplomacy 1959, Chinatown 1999) but stayed niche; no video game makes free negotiation the core pillar.
- **🟥 Roblox sketch — *"The Commons"*:** A shared persistent valley. Each player has private goals (build a mill, raise a herd) but every resource — water, timber, the bridge — is co-owned. The **whole game is the negotiation server**: proposing splits, forming temporary pacts, trading turns at the well. No combat, no elimination — the tension is purely social. Roblox supplies the one missing ingredient (rooms full of real people), voice/age-verified chat carries the deals, and the persistent server means reputations follow you across sessions. Maps directly onto Roblox's named "social co-opetition" demand. **[SPECULATION on the design; SOURCED on the gap & demand]**

---

#### 2. **Sowing / redistribution** (the mancala verb) as a live multiplayer core
- **The idea:** The hand-scoop-and-sow mechanic of mancala — pick up a pile, redistribute it counter-clockwise, capture by where you land. **Bao** (East-African Swahili mancala) is regarded as the most strategically deep variant (two phases, relay/bidirectional sowing) and has *resisted* clean digitization — only niche apps and one obscure Steam title exist. **[SOURCED]** (Wikipedia: Bao; ancientgames.org)
- **The 1935 test:** It's literally **the oldest board mechanic on Earth** (Senet/mancala lineage, millennia old). The "redistribute a pile and watch consequences cascade" verb is satisfying and almost absent from video games.
- **🟥 Roblox sketch — *"Sow"*:** Keep the tactile primal verb (grab a glowing pile, fling seeds around a ring, captures pop) but layer Roblox's strength: a **persistent ladder + spectator tables** where a whole server watches live 1v1s, bets cosmetic seeds, and climbs regional leaderboards (huge in APAC where mancala/congkak is folk-familiar). Language-light, mobile-perfect, all-ages.

---

#### 3. **Asymmetric "one-vs-many hunt"** + sound-based folk pursuit — at scale
- **The idea:** Two structurally *different* roles. Ancient board form: **Tafl/Hnefatafl** (a king + defenders escaping a larger attacking force). Ancient *playground* form: **Marco Polo** (echolocation), **Sardines** (inverse hide-and-seek — finders join the hidden cluster), **Kabaddi** (breath-held raids). Asymmetric design is "quite rare… two completely different experiences for two players," because balance is hard — the *specific, citable* reason the space is empty rather than mere neglect. **[SOURCED]** (gamedeveloper.com asymmetry; Wikipedia: Tafl / Hide-and-seek / Marco Polo)
- **The 1935 test:** Sardines is documented as "Smee" from a **1931** source; Kabaddi is an ancient codified sport; Tafl predates chess in Northern Europe (and was *lost* before its rules were written down — an entire genre humanity invented, mislaid, and is still re-deriving). **[SOURCED]**
- **🟥 Roblox sketch — *"Sardine Town"*:** Scale the folk structure to **a 100-player server** — the one form research found genuinely *unbuilt* (social deduction & hunt games stay small-group). One hidden "seed" player; finders who catch them *join* the hidden cluster, so the hunted team silently grows while the map gossips about who's already flipped. Sound (proximity voice = the Marco-Polo echolocation layer), no text barrier, mobile-friendly. Folk-familiar worldwide.

---

### TIER 2 — Strong: a clean primal mechanic, lightly explored, needs the right wrapper

---

#### 4. **Loop / "antenna" capture** — the Surakarta mechanic
- **The idea:** In the Indonesian game **Surakarta**, you capture *only* by travelling around looping tracks at the board's corners and landing on an enemy — a mechanic Wikipedia calls "possibly unique… not known to exist in any other recorded board game." A satisfying capture verb essentially absent from all of digital design. **[SOURCED]** (Wikipedia: Surakarta)
- **The 1935 test:** A loop drawn on any board; nothing modern about it.
- **🟥 Roblox sketch:** The visual is *made* for a 3D engine — pieces physically whip around glowing loop-rails to strike. Pure, readable, juicy spectacle; a clean competitive 1v1 + tournament mode. Strong "easy to watch, hard to master" shape.

#### 5. **Caregiving / tending** as a *competitive or persistent-multiplayer* loop
- **The idea:** Tending is proven (Tamagotchi 1996, Animal Crossing) but trapped in solo/cozy niches — almost never the *primary competitive or social* verb. Koster's filter rejects "care" because it generates few adversarial situations. **[SOURCED]** (marygeorgescu.com; raphkoster.com)
- **The 1935 test:** Raising an animal, nursing a garden — timeless; the *only* novelty is making it the headline multiplayer loop.
- **🟥 Roblox sketch:** Roblox already half-discovered this — *Grow a Garden* was the **fastest experience ever to 1B visits (33 days)**. The unexploited move is care as a *relational* loop, not a numbers-go-up idle: you tend things *for each other*, gift cuttings, co-raise a shared creature whose mood reflects the whole server's attention. Turns "care" social and persistent. **[SOURCED on Grow a Garden's scale]**

#### 6. **Non-cube randomizers** — stick/bean race-gambling games
- **The idea:** A cluster of ancient games built on randomizers that *aren't* six-sided dice: **Daldøs** (4-sided long stick die; race+capture; essentially *undigitized* — the cleanest "no known digital form" case in the sweep), **Patolli** (Aztec bean-dice gambling race), **Liubo** (Han-dynasty — so old its *rules are lost*, making the design space genuinely open). **[SOURCED, with absence-of-evidence caveat on Daldøs]** (Wikipedia: Daldøs / Patolli / Liubo; BGG; liubolab.itch.io)
- **The 1935 test:** These literally existed centuries-to-millennia ago; the gap is purely a *definitive modern form*.
- **🟥 Roblox sketch:** A "folk-casino" hub of stick/bean-cast race games with **cosmetic-stake betting and live tables** — the casual social-gambling loop (cf. Roblox's bingo demand) minus money, plus the satisfying physical *cast* of sticks the engine can make tactile. A respectful "lost games of the world" framing also gives it cultural-localization hooks for international growth.

---

### TIER 3 — Provocative: more speculative, but high-ceiling "obvious in hindsight" bets

---

#### 7. **Inverted / absent win conditions** — games you try to *lose*, or define your own goal
- Misère play (lowest score wins) and goal-less games (e.g. *Endurance* — "there is no victory… *you* decide what winning is") are explicitly "underexplored in mainstream design." **[SOURCED]** (medium.com/understanding-games; gamedeveloper.com victory-conditions)
- **🟥 Roblox sketch:** A party game where the scoreboard *inverts* without warning — the round you thought you were winning flips to "last place takes the crown." Cheap to build, endlessly clippable, perfect for Roblox's social-party niche. **[SPECULATION on design]**

#### 8. **Cozy + competitive** — the empty quadrant
- Daniel Cook frames the axis: mainstream multiplayer runs on "limited resources, high stakes, hazardous worlds"; the untapped quadrant uses "abundance, safety, reprieve" *with* real competition. A few exist (Quilts & Cats of Calico) but it's "relatively niche" with no defining title. **[SOURCED]** (lostgarden.com/cozy-games)
- **🟥 Roblox sketch:** Ranked ladder play where you compete on *beauty/creativity* (best-arranged garden, coziest room) judged by peer vote — competition without aggression. Fits Roblox's *Dress to Impress* lineage and the "create *with*/against others" co-opetition demand.

#### 9. **Jobs-as-play, re-framed as social networks** (the honest version)
> **[CORRECTED]** Several of my initial guesses are *already done*: shopkeeper/haggling (*Potionomics*), lighthouse keeper, ferryman, postman (*Death Stranding*), matchmaker (*Kitty Powers'*) all have indie titles. The accurate gap is narrower:
- **Matchmaker-as-*gossip-network*** (the historical *shadchan* brokered marriages via "gossip and discretion") — the *social-network* framing has no game. **[SOURCED on the practice; SPECULATION on the gap]** (freakonomics.com/matchmakers)
- Roles like **ferryman/postman as a *multiplayer social* role** (carrying messages and rumors between real players) rather than a solo courier — unbuilt.
- **🟥 Roblox sketch:** A town where players *are* the infrastructure — one ferries goods, one carries letters, one brokers introductions — and the fun is the **emergent rumor/economy network** between real people. Roblox's persistent social servers are uniquely suited; nobody has made the "be the connective tissue of a living town" game.

---

## Honest caveats (the adversarial pass)

- **"No digital form" is usually too strong.** Most famous folk games (Oware, Hnefatafl, Nine Men's Morris, Surakarta) *do* have niche apps. The accurate claim is **"no *definitive, mass-market* form."** Genuinely form-*less* cases are narrow: **Daldøs** (≈undigitized, absence-of-evidence), **Liubo** (rules unrecoverable), and **Kabaddi/gilli-danda** (no good video game despite huge regional play). **[SOURCED]**
- **Several "gaps" are near-misses, not voids** — cohabitive games, haggling, cozy-competitive, 100-player social deduction all have *prototypes*; the opportunity is "no canonical title," not "first ever."
- **Roblox's technical friction is real:** event-driven client-server architecture + mandatory mobile performance make *deep simulation* expensive — which is *why* these gaps persist, and why the winning ideas above are mechanically **simple, social, and language-light** rather than simulation-heavy. **[MEDIUM confidence — partly forum-sourced]**

## If you build one thing
The highest-leverage bet that satisfies *every* constraint (primal · 1935-able · all-ages · international · language-light · plays to Roblox's social/persistent strengths · sits in a funded, demand-proven gap) is a **TIER 1** idea: **#1 Cohabitive "The Commons"** (if you want genuinely novel) or **#3 "Sardine Town"** (if you want proven-folk-familiar with the clearest unbuilt-at-scale evidence).
